turn_prompts:
Start a new fenced authoring conversation, read validation_environment_contract and validation_repair_context first, then read the prior candidate snapshot, validation_receipt, verification_contract, and any critic findings. Critic findings are optional; validation_repair_context is the primary diagnosis. In the authoring workspace, source/ is read-only and task/ is the only writable candidate directory; write only the fixed candidate files under task/. After each focused correction, call harbor_validate_candidate. A rejected receipt returns bounded diagnostics; apply the next focused correction and call again in the same turn until the receipt passes or the repair budget is exhausted. Only provision Debian packages in environment/Dockerfile when the frozen task genuinely requires them. Whenever apt-get is used, switch the default Debian APT sources from HTTP to HTTPS before apt-get update exactly with this guarded command. Bookworm images may ship either /etc/apt/sources.list or deb822 /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources; a missing file must never fail the build:
RUN if [ -f /etc/apt/sources.list ]; then sed -i 's|^deb http://|deb https://|; s|^deb-src http://|deb-src https://|' /etc/apt/sources.list; fi; for f in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then sed -i 's|^URIs: http://|URIs: https://|' "$f"; fi; done
Never use sed alternation or \1 backreference expressions for this switch; the controlled build network permits HTTPS egress only. When the frozen VerificationContract invokes test.sh through sh, both test.sh and solution/solve.sh must be POSIX sh compatible: do not use set -o pipefail, bash arrays, [[, or other Bash-only syntax. task.toml must keep the Harbor TaskConfig contract: [metadata] with code_lang, task_type, application, is_0_to_1, github_url, and commit_id; [task] with a valid org/name name and non-empty description; [environment] with positive build_timeout_sec, network_mode = "no-network", and workdir = "/workspace/source"; [verifier] with positive timeout_sec. tests_analysis.json must remain the strict harbor.standard-authoring-tests-analysis.v2 JSON with unique requirement_ids and non-empty provided_information, theoretical_path, and passing_evidence. When the latest receipt rejects only because tests/test.sh validate_log requires "test result: ok." from a binary that ran no tests, fix validate_log itself: browser-wasm test runners print "test result: ok." only for binaries that report "running N tests" with N at least 1, so pure helper modules with no tests (for example tests/utils.rs) never print that line. Require "test result: ok." only for sections matching "running [1-9][0-9]* tests" and never from binaries with no test output.

Read validation_repair_context before critic findings; critic findings are optional context only. Correct the documented failing layer in the candidate workspace, preserving validation_environment_contract: validator /source and /task are read-only, /work is the writable copy where solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh operate. Call harbor_validate_candidate to create the next immutable snapshot and receipt; if the receipt rejects, correct the failing layer again and validate within the same turn.

If validation remains rejected, compare validation_repair_context, repair_guidance, the current candidate, the frozen VerificationContract, baseline behavior, and Oracle behavior. Apply one focused correction and call harbor_validate_candidate; if it still rejects, apply the next focused correction and validate again in the same turn. Do not alter frozen source inputs, source/, /source, or the verifier contract.

Use validation_repair_context to repair the narrow failing layer: layout, environment provisioning, baseline, Oracle, coverage, or integrity. Runtime validation is no-network with a read-only root filesystem, so keep runtime writes under /work or /tmp/harbor-* and keep scripts POSIX sh when the contract invokes them through sh, then validate the replacement candidate and re-validate in the same turn after each focused correction.

Only change environment/Dockerfile when validation_repair_context identifies an environment-layer failure and the latest receipt shows environment_build failed; if any receipt shows environment provisioning succeeded (host_candidate_verify or any earlier repair receipt), keep environment/Dockerfile byte-identical and repair only the failing code/test layer. When provisioning is genuinely required for Rust/Cargo browser-wasm failures, provision generic wasm/browser tools in environment/Dockerfile during Docker build; runtime dependencies must come from the pinned base image, repository vendor tree, or another frozen input. Set CARGO_HOME=/work/.cargo-home and CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/work/.cargo-target, and do not copy full Cargo registry or target caches into limited /tmp. When the frozen Cargo.lock pins a wasm-bindgen version whose CLI must be built from source, install that CLI with a rust toolchain era-compatible with the pinned version (for example rust 1.80.0 for wasm-bindgen 0.2.87) instead of the base-image default rustc, and prefer the pinned crate's own --locked resolution or the official release binaries when the source build fails.

Re-read validation_repair_context and the most recent receipt before changing files. Preserve every successful constraint while correcting only the remaining failure, and call harbor_validate_candidate after the repair; a rejected receipt allows one further focused correction and re-validation within the same turn.

Continue the bounded repair loop from the latest immutable candidate and validation_repair_context. Do not hide failures, bypass the verifier, or substitute a different repository, command, or source revision; validate each next focused correction immediately and keep correcting and re-validating in the same turn while a rejected receipt leaves repair budget.

Use the final available repair turn only for a correction supported by validation_repair_context, repair_guidance, and the latest receipt. Check that instruction, task metadata, environment, solution, test script, and tests analysis agree with the frozen task and verification contracts, then call harbor_validate_candidate and rely on its immutable receipt; if it rejects, apply one final focused correction and validate again in this same turn while budget remains. A passing receipt ends the repair loop.
